title: Plotting from pandas
summary: Series.plot and DataFrame.plot: one call from a table to a chart, still with an Axes you control.

steps.title: `.plot` on a Series or DataFrame
body: pandas wraps matplotlib: `.plot()` on a Series or DataFrame draws it and **returns the Axes**.
ax = s.plot(kind="bar", title="Sales")    # index becomes the x axis
df.plot(x="month", y=["north", "south"])  # one line per column, legend included

steps.explain: pandas returns a matplotlib `Axes`, draws one line per column, labels the x axis with the `x` column's name and adds a legend for you.

steps.prompt: Plot the top regions as horizontal bars into the right-hand panel.

steps.title: A Series to a bar chart
prompt: Write `plot_counts(items)` where `items` is a pandas Series of product names (one per order). Count them with
`value_counts()` (most common first) and plot the counts as a bar chart with pandas, titled `Orders per product`.

steps.prompt: When is plain matplotlib a better choice than `df.plot`?
options: When you need full control of every artist, or the data is not already shaped as one column per series
Only when saving the chart to a file
When the DataFrame has an index
steps.explain: `df.plot` is great for quick charts of tidy summaries. For unusual layouts or annotations you drop down to the Axes it returns, or to matplotlib directly. They mix freely.

steps.title: Shape the table, then plot
body: pandas plots *columns* as series and the *index* as the x axis. So most of the work is shaping the table:
If the chart looks wrong, look at the table you are plotting first.

steps.title: Monthly revenue by region
prompt: Write `plot_by_region(df)` where `df` has `month`, `region` and `revenue` (several orders per month and region).
Pivot it to one row per month and one column per region (sum of revenue, missing as 0), plot it with pandas as
lines, set the title `Revenue by region` and y label `Revenue`, and return the Axes.
solution: wide = df.pivot_table(index="month", columns="region", values="revenue", aggfunc="sum", fill_value=0)
template: Dojo.eq("legend", ["N", "S"], [t.get_text() for t in dojo_ax.get_legend().get_texts()] if dojo_ax.get_legend() else [])
